short: Synergistic enhanced thermal conductivity of polydimethylsil
title: Synergistic enhanced thermal conductivity of polydimethylsiloxane composites via introducing SCF and hetero-structured GB@rGO hybrid fillers

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Electronic devices need flexible thermal interface materials with high thermal conductivity. Hollow core-shell GB@rGO filling gaps of a compressed SCF network should cut heat dissipation and raise lambda synergistically.
states.detail: Absorbed: s1 (HYP/need), s2 (HYP/hypothesis), s3 (DES/base_system), s4 (DES/modification), s5 (DES/variable_sweep), s6 (DES/route), s7 (PRC/synthesis), s8 (PRC/forming)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: GB spheres carry a wrinkled rGO sheet coating after thermal reduction. SCFs lie in-plane, perpendicular to the compression axis, overlapping into an interlaced network.
states.detail: Absorbed: s9 (STR/microstructure/distribution), s11 (STR/microstructure/orientation), s25 (STR/microstructure/distribution), s12 (STR/microstructure/distribution), s26 (STR/microstructure/distribution)

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: GB@rGO in narrow network gaps squeezes out low-lambda PDMS, so SCF paths conduct better (volume exclusion). Conducting rGO shell over an insulating glass-air core limits heat dissipation from the SCF network.
states.detail: Absorbed: s13 (MEC/pathway), s27 (MEC/pathway), s14 (PRP/value), s15 (PRP/value). Premises: Pure PDMS conducts heat poorly (0.27 W/m K), so matrix left in network gaps limits heat transfer; Glass-bubble interior (glass and air) is thermally insulating while the rGO shell conducts heat

states.title: Performance state
states.head: On a heated ceramic plate the 1 wt% composite keeps the plate coolest among the GB@rGO contents. As a CPU TIM the composite holds the core about 5 C cooler than commercial thermal grease

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Compression-assembled SCF network plus 1 wt% GB@rGO synergistically raises PDMS lambda to about 23.4 W/m K (85.7x)

nodes.title: MICRO, F3, F5
nodes.head: Bare GB spheres are smooth; GB@GO and GB@rGO spheres carry wrinkled sheet patches, denser on GB@rGO. Fibres lie mostly in the sheet plane in the out-of-plane sections, more obliquely at 0.4-0.6 mm.
nodes.solves: GB spheres carry a wrinkled rGO sheet coating after thermal reduction

nodes.title: IR, F4, F7, F9
nodes.head: GB@rGO FTIR trace still carries labelled C=O and O-H bands, though the text says they disappear. Bands above 1200 cm-1 are weaker on GB@rGO than on GB@GO; Si-O-Si near 1000 cm-1 dominates both.
nodes.op: compare across conditions, correlate across series, cross check consistency, read trend
nodes.note: bands are weak on GB@rGO but marked by the authors wide scan only, no O/C ratio given; GB SiO2 also contributes O1s and Si2p on GB@rGO F9b-d LED loop currents 0.07 (Cu), 0.04 (0 wt%), 0.06 mA (1 wt%) at 5.60 V agree sigma 824 vs 651 S/m; lambda (0.1 mm) ~15.5 vs ~22.5 W/m K; sample thickness for sigma not stated
nodes.detail: o5: GB@rGO FTIR trace still carries labelled C=O and O-H bands, though the text says they disappear; o6: Bands above 1200 cm-1 are weaker on GB@rGO than on GB@GO; Si-O-Si near 1000 cm-1 dominates both; o7: O1s peak relative to C1s is smaller on GB@rGO than on GO; o8: Residual mass at 900 C: GB ~99%, GB@rGO ~91%, GB@GO ~88%, GO ~44%; o22: Electrical conductivity: 651, 1330, 866, 824, 480 S/m at 0, 1, 2, 4, 6 wt% GB@rGO; o25: Sigma at 2 and 4 wt% exceeds 0 wt%, while lambda at 4 wt% is far below 0 wt%: the two do not co-vary

nodes.note: 2-mm bars near 1 W/m K (text 0.367); 3D bars read ~1 W/m K above text values
nodes.detail: o13: Lambda increases at every content as thickness goes 2 -> 0.4 -> 0.2 -> 0.1 mm

nodes.title: evidence, F7
nodes.head: At 0.1 mm lambda ranks 1 wt% (~24) > 2 wt% (~23) > 0 wt% (~22.5) > 4 wt% (~15.5); at 0.2 mm 1 wt% also leads. At 0.4 mm the 1 wt% bar is at or below 0 wt% in both lambda and TCE
nodes.solves: 1 wt% GB@rGO gives the highest lambda at 0.1-0.2 mm (about 23-24 W/m K); 4 wt% lowers it
nodes.note: TCE panel b gives the same ranking (~88x at 0.1 mm, 1 wt%; text 85.72x); at 0.2 mm 2 wt% sits below 0 wt%; 6 wt% absent from F7a/b despite the sweep lambda ~12.7 vs ~13.1; TCE ~45 vs ~46; the 1-wt% optimum holds only at 0.1-0.2 mm

nodes.title: MECH:tensile, F10
nodes.head: Elongation and tensile strength drop with GB@rGO content; at 0.1 mm strength ~1.5 -> ~1.1 (1 wt%) -> ~0.8 MPa (6 wt%). Sheet is folded into a bow, tetrahedron and other shapes.
nodes.note: legends say 'rGO@GB'; the ~25-30% strength loss at 1 wt% is more than the text's 'slight' bend angle drawn as 60 deg in F10d vs 120 deg in text; caption names panel (e), figure has (d)
